quest.title: "Outlander Brigade!"
quest.description: Xavier seems to be busy shooting a new film...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Furuta
dialogues.text: Oh, hello. It's been a while since I saw you last.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Is that so? I must be getting on in years. My memory just isn't what it used to be.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Ah me! Not only is my memory like a sieve, but I'm finding myself more and more puzzled by what the younger folk are interested in.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Before, a young'un from Fontaine came here, saying that he was making a "film," and chatted on and on with the master of the house.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Goodness, and he kept saying, um... "Dear." Throwing around a word like that all willy-nilly, does he have no shame?

choices.text: I think I know this person.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Yes, that's him! He mentioned you as well.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: It sounded like he had received funds from the Tenryou Commission and finally managed to make a film, but the commission wasn't satisfied with the result.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: But he wanted to stick with it, so he came to us, the commission in charge of the humanities and arts, for help.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: I didn't expect the master to agree to this, let alone to send Koharu to help. Is this film really so interesting? This is all completely beyond me.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Still, since the master agreed, I should not pass judgment as a mere butler.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: But after thinking it over, I'm still worried about Koharu.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: That's right. I can tell that Koharu isn't too fond of this jabbering outlander.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: She's always strictly obeyed the commands of the master and lady and would never deliberately disobey an order, but that child lacks training and composure.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: That outlander is a bit too... unreserved. If he ruffles Koharu's feathers and she can't restrain herself again, there'll be trouble.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Koharu's training hasn't been brief by any means, and while her skills are far from perfect, she could easily knock someone lacking in fighting skills out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Who is Koharu, anyway?

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Well, who do you think Koharu and I are?

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Whatever answer you have in mind, all you need to know is that we're absolutely loyal to the Yashiro Commission and the Kamisato Clan.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Since you know the boy and have earned the trust of the entire house, a humble housekeeper such as myself is naturally at ease when it comes to you.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: If you could find the time to go see how that film is coming along, I'd be eternally grateful.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure thing.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: I seem to recall that he took a group of people to an island south of here. Anyway, thanks for letting me talk your ear off for this long.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Please come back when you have the time. The entire house would be honored.

choices.text: Isn't Koharu a servant of the Kamisato Clan?
It's true, I haven't been back for a while now.

response.speaker: Furuta
response.text: Haha, I knew it. Now, I may be getting on in years and losing my memory, but at least I didn't forget that.

talks.objective: Learn about the progress of Xavier's film shoot

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: This is the 11th time. I just don't get it.

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: Ugh... Just say it. What was the problem this time?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The problem this time, Ms. Koharu, is that your performance just now was completely passionless.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: When I wrote those lines, my heart was bursting with an... an empty yet fervent passion, yes, empty yet fervent.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I need you to be more patient. Use your voice to express this rich emotion.

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: Huh? An "empty yet fervent passion"? What does that even mean?

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, didn't the casting call say that the script was written by a famous writer?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: That's absolutely right! This story was adapted from a novel written by the renowned author Kayabuki Ikkei. And who adapted it, you might ask? None other than myself.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ms. Koharu, Mr. Sasano, I am very sorry for making you both go over this so many times.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: But it's all worth it for the sake of artistic perfection. As such, I hope that...

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: Hold on, I only know one Kayabuki Ikkei, and everything he submitted to the Yae Publishing House always got rejected.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: But he wouldn't accept that, so he started publishing his own novels, but not a single one sold in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: Don't tell me that we've been put through the wringer 11 times for something that guy wrote?

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: Argh! I've had enough of this nonsense!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err, that doesn't look good. Seems like Koharu's seconds away from flying off the handle.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go say hello.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... So, Xavier, are you guys filming?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Long time no see.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, my dear friends! How marvelous it is to see familiar faces at a time like this.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: As you can see, following "The Seventh Samurai," I finally came up with a way to secure the necessary resources to shoot another film.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The lead role hasn't been decided yet, but thanks to Lord Kamisato's generosity, the funds, props, and nearly all the other early-stage problems have already been taken care of.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: If you don't mind, could I ask if you maybe, possibly, at all remember our agreement from before?

response.speaker: Koharu
response.text: #Eh, {NICKNAME}'s a friend of the Yashiro Commissioner. So you all know each other?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #That's right, {NICKNAME} was the first friend I made in Inazuma. The Fatui who dumped a bunch of work on me and those non-communicative samurai don't count.

response.speaker: Koharu
response.text: #If you made friends with {NICKNAME}, I guess you can't be all bad.

response.speaker: Sasano
response.text: Well, it seems like Xavier's got some chops after all...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're very good friends.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: You really think so? Even though I've never said so, I for my part have considered you a true friend right from the start.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: You aren't just my "dear friend," you're my esteemed, reliable, true friend.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Of course, of course! And here you are right at this most dire moment, like an oasis in the deserts of Sumeru — precious and timely.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Well, so long as, as per our previous agreement, you remain willing to play the role of the {M#male}{F#female} lead in my new film.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #So, what do you say? Will you be my... {M#male}{F#female} lead?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I would be honored.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon can attest to {NICKNAME}'s ability to improvise! We've traveled together long enough, after all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Getting {M#him}{F#her} to be the main character is definitely a win for you, Xavier.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Absolutely! I have no doubt of that. Well then, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}, here are the scripts for the next two scenes.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Your scenes are Act I, Scene II and III. <color=#00E1FFFF>I've highlighted your lines, so please take note of them</color>.

response.speaker: Sasano
response.text: Well, it took this much effort to find the right person for the lead role... I might as well give this one more try.

response.speaker: Koharu
response.text: Ugh... Fine, then I will too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Everything looks so official! Paimon's looking forward to watching your performance, {NICKNAME}. Hee-hee~

choices.text: You don't have to call me any of that.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ah, of course, of course — it's already been a long time since then, after all. You must've had many other important matters to take care of, so it's completely understandable that our first meeting didn't leave an impression.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Don't worry, I'm not surprised or disappointed. Really.

talks.objective: Talk to Xavier to begin the shoot

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Good, good! Then let's begin.

talks.objective: Complete the "Act I, Scene II" film shoot
Complete the "Act I, Scene II" film shoot

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm not ready yet.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: No problem at all. We still have time. Let's begin once you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: Excuse me, but did you come to oversee the filming at my master's request?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was Furuta who was a little worried about you.

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: She was? I, uh... I guess I've not grown up enough yet if I'm still making her worry.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: This won't do. If this continues, we won't have a chance against... them.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Smoother, Mr. Sasano, smoother!

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: (These lines are just so awkward, though.)

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: We'll have to sacrifice ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: With feeling, Ms. Koharu! Once more with feeling!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But I won't lose like this.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Very nice! Excellent performance, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Mr. Sasano, Ms. Koharu, you two need to go over our script. The next scene is between you two. We need to do better than this!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, we have a lot of battle scenes up next, so you'll need to complete them with the extras.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Try to use the flashiest moves you can. I have a lot of faith in your abilities — I know your performance will be stellar.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: No, no, no, that's not the line here! Do you still remember it?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I think you still need a little more time to memorize your lines.

choices.text: What am I supposed to say again?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: ...Mr. Sasano, Ms. Koharu, I'm disappointed in both of you.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The difference between these crude shots and a true film is like... like Mondstadt's Dandelion Wine and Apple Cider — one is alcohol, one isn't. They simply aren't the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Heavens above, I just don't even know how to describe it.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: You can't remember your lines, your readings are all over the place, and you're not giving me any emotion! How am I supposed to work with that?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: This is a crime, a crime against art. This can't go on, my friends.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: I'm really sorry that you're so disappointed, but I don't plan to continue taking part in this.

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: You can reprimand or punish me, but I'm not going to keep doing this either.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Mr. Sasano?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I mean, I know that there have been some issues with these performances, but it's nothing a few more rehearsals can't fix!

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: There's no need. We could practice a hundred times and I still wouldn't understand what your script is about.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: I share the sentiment. Why would these two characters suddenly sacrifice themselves and run off to where the enemy is?

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: No matter how you look at it, it just doesn't make any sense. They are just dragging the main character down.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: And the lines at the end are so awkward I feel embarrassed just reading them.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: In short, I quit. Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Koharu
dialogues.text: Yup. That's that, then.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Eh? How could you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: With Sasano and Koharu gone, we shan't have enough actors to continue filming! This is bad...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There, there. It's okay.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah, I am so sorry. Your efforts... I fear they shall go to waste now.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I'm just... I confess, I'm at a loss for words. I'm going to <color=#00E1FFFF>Uyuu Restaurant</color> for a moment. I need to be alone. I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: We'll talk about this matter the next time we meet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now Xavier's gone too. Seems like he's in pretty bad shape.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He must be taking the argument they had earlier really hard. Do you think we should go cheer him up a bit?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm... Paimon remembers him mentioning <color=#00E1FFFF>Uyuu Restaurant</color>. If you think we should go, then let's go look for him.

choices.text: Let's think of a way to remedy this situation.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Heh, you found me. *burp*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeesh, it reeks of booze around here. You're drunk, aren't you, Xavier?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: D—Don't say that. It's ru... ruining the vibe! You sound like my mom. *burp* Come on, lesh drink together.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe some other time.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Huh? What kinda friend are you? You're no fun.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Wasn't it just, um, right, when we were filming. I was... being questioned. Madly so! Yesh!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Actually, I don't blame Ms. Koharu. *burp* Or Mr. Sasano. They were very cooperative at first.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: That is to say, or I think that is to say, it's probably 'cause I'm, um, not that talented.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: You! You really are a good person, ya know that? You're so, so good. Here, lemme give you a hug!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, a minute ago you were drunk as a skunk! You're not taking advantage of the situation to get chummy with us, are you?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: You know that film I worked so hard on before? Well, the higher-ups at the Tenryou Commission didn't like it too much.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: They didn't come right out and say it, but they were totally silent, which means they didn't approve.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But I refuse to accept this. I refuse!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: This time, I was able to get funding from Lord Kamisato to make this film, so I... I must take this seriously! Don't you think?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: My dearest, most adored good friend, you're closer to me than a sibling, so I'll tell you something about me: I'm an engineer.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But I think I can be more than an engineer. I've read lots of books, and I can write stuff.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I could... I could also be a film writer, an actor, a director!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I'm not talking outta my hat here, I could rea... really do it. Don't you believe me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I believe you.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Great! I would kiss you if I could, but I drank a smidge too much... and my breath stinks.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Don't get the wrong idea, {NICKNAME}, I just think you're truly my most dearest and bestest friend.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: My best friend, I must treat you to a meal today, and I won't take no for an answer.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: My dear fellow, we order food from you, correct? Come, my friend, order whatever you'd like.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: That's all? No, no, no, unacceptable. You are my best friend! The best friend of Xavier, man of Fontaine!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Being stingy with my friends would damage my character, and I am, if nothing else, a person of character!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: My dear sir, we'll have the Tri-Flavored Skewer, Tonkotsu Ramen, and whatever else you serve here.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Understood. Erika, one of everything for this table.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Soon after, shop owner Okazaki Rikuto piles your table high with food.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Dear {NICKNAME}, dear Paimon, now this is what I call a real meal!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Come, let's eat. For our dreams!

choices.text: I think you've had a little too much drink.
You just need a little more experience.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ooh, wait, no — I remember you saying that you wanted to give up drinking. You gotta stay on that wagon, okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: When did I say that...?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: It musta been in my dream.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: *burp*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, you're a good guy, Xavier! You're Paimon's best friend! Well... one of them, anyway!

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: How was everything?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Simply divine! I could taste the lake in your rice and fish. That sweet and delicate aroma is just like what I'd have in my hometown of Petrichor.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Haha, is that so? I'm glad you liked it.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Now, I didn't mean to eavesdrop, but this film you mentioned sounds very interesting indeed. Could you tell me more about it, if you wouldn't mind?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Xavier explain the film to Okazaki Rikuto and show him the script as well.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Ooh, so this outlander has the resolve to stand up and fight when things get tough. Impressive.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: But to be honest, there is so little thought or hesitation involved here that this person barely seems human at all.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: When they meet an enemy they can't beat, they summon up the courage to charge anyway... and they actually triumph. That sort of daring is actually rather frightening.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: You're still young, Mr. Xavier. I take it that you've never experienced such life-threatening situations before?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Certainly not "life-threatening," no. But is this the reason why my script has been criticized? Hmm...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Well, let me put it this way. Is having an identical experience first strictly necessary to writing a good story?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: From what I understand, quite a number of great authors are homebodies.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Besides, I find this no-nonsense, swords-drawn approach very Inazuma-esque.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Since I've come to Inazuma, I should make some films with that Inazuma flair.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Mr. Kayabuki's original work was also in this style, and in order to preserve these unique elements, I've decided to honor the source.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Ah, you mean Kayabuki Ikkei? An interesting lad, to be sure.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Xavier, I'm moved by your dedication to film. I can't help but be reminded of a story I once heard...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ah! Sitting in a restaurant, eating, and listening to stories like this is also so... so Inazuma! I love it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hm... Om nom nom nom~ You guys go on, Paimon's just gonna finish up over here first...

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Long, long ago, there lived someone named Seishimaru.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Seishimaru was born to samurai parents who worked for powerful people. Well, they weren't very powerful themselves, but they weren't too bad, either.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: But these parents seemingly made a strange error in their work, incurring punishment and eventually submitting to their execution.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Unable to accept their deaths, Seishimaru toiled to find the samurai family that carried out the sentence.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Truth be told, the responsible party did everything by the book, and the family serving as executioner normally shouldn't have been blamed for the sentence they were ordered to carry out.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: This family was also acquainted with Seishimaru's... Goodness me, this story's pretty hard to tell without naming names.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: For now, suppose that the family responsible was the Wakayama Clan. To all the good people in Inazuma named Wakayama, please don't hate me for this...

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Ah, as I was saying... Blinded by hatred, Seishimaru decided to take revenge on the Wakayamas.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: But by then, the person who had personally beheaded Seishimaru's parents had already passed away, leaving the eldest son in charge of the Wakayama estate.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: This person happened to also be Seishimaru's childhood friend. But now, they had become enemies.

choices.text: This is a story of friends becoming foes.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Very clever, you hit the nail on the head.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows, Paimon knows! Something awful's gonna happen next. It doesn't matter if it's Mondstadt, Liyue, or Inazuma, it's always the same wherever you go.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Hehe, indeed, there is nothing new under the sun. People always lose themselves due to the same old things. I suppose there are plenty of stories like this one in Fontaine too.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Anyway, before any action was taken, Seishimaru, supposedly remembering the old days, took out a Temari and a sword and let the eldest son of the Wakayama family choose between them.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: What does that mean?

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Now, how should I know what Seishimaru was thinking? Still, I think that the Temari and sword represented life and death respectively.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Having made the wrong choice, the Wakayama's eldest son had no choice but to accept being pursued and slain by Seishimaru. What an ill-fated lad.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: But before Seishimaru could even come knocking at his door, an illness took him.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: I don't know if that was lucky or unlucky. Dying of an illness and being killed both mean dying either way, so who knows which would have been better?

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: It's hard not to blame Seishimaru for his death. If it weren't for the former's being bent on revenge, the latter wouldn't have needed to lay low until he fell ill.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: After that, the younger Wakayama child immediately sought vengeance. Good grief, the cycle never ends, does it?

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Seishimaru was forced into hiding in the mountains before eventually disappearing.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Some say Seishimaru fled in fear of the Wakayamas, while others say he let himself sink to the depths of the ocean to quench his burning hatred.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Whichever ending you wish to believe, no one ever saw Seishimaru again.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: To this day, such fretful matters as hate and shame should all have flowed into the ley lines with Seishimaru's death.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Since this whole dispute has lost its source, just take "and all was well again" to be this story's ending.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: That's... it? So, not even you know where this Seishimaru went?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, yeah! All was *not* well at all! What kind of ending is that?

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: I'm sorry, but that's how the part I heard ends. After all, it's a tale that's been spread to many places, so such vagueness is unavoidable.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Back to the issue — you see, Mr. Xavier? You need a story with an ending that leaves people wanting more.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: ...Mr. Okazaki, I must say that you are indeed a gentleman of great insight.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I wouldn't be surprised if the legend of Seishimaru took place in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Especially one of the legend's endings, the one where Seishimaru disappears to put an end to his hatred. That sounds just like what a friend of mine from Sumeru would do.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I want to thank you for your kindness and the nudge you've given me, and not just through this story — your unique way of giving advice has given me just the inspiration I needed.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I think I know what was missing from my film before.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Thank you, Mr. Okazaki. This is for the meal.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: If I can manage to write an even better script, I'll come back to offer you my most solemn gratitude.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Haha, tell you what, I really envy your youth and drive, Traveler.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: To be able to befriend such a person is a gift from the gods. You must be a special person as well to have been so blessed.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Good things surely await you and Mr. Xavier.

choices.text: This story about a family's fall following punishment from above... I've heard tales like these before.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Looks like our young friend here is well-read!

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Officials are privileged, but they also have responsibilities, and mistakes must be punished. We have our own rules here in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: It's not unheard of for an official to slip up and fall into ruin. But you don't seem surprised at all. You must have a wide circle of friends.

response.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
response.text: Since this isn't surprising to you, I'm afraid that the fallout between Seishimaru and the son of the Wakayamas will be equally predictable.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: We're honored that you appreciate Erika's work so much. It's only right that we extend our opening hours for you.

dialogues.speaker: Okazaki Rikuto
dialogues.text: After you leave, we'll tidy up a little, then have Erika go take a rest.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The story is quite complete, but it's lacking some emotional turmoil. Hmm...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Heavens forgive me, I'm a real souse this morning, I am. I left my friend in the restaurant after completely forgetting about them!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But I think I can now write an all-new, presentable script and give this one more shot. It'll definitely work this time. No, I'll make it work.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Please allow me a little more time. Just one day will suffice.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: *sigh*... But it's going to be tricky with those two actors. Ms. Koharu and Mr. Sasano don't seem keen on trying again.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But I can't blame them either. I'll just have to think of something when the time comes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can I help in any way?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: No, no, no, I couldn't ask for anything more comforting than having you here to listen to me vent.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #My dear {NICKNAME}, you are indeed a great listener.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ms. Paimon, if my behavior was at all untoward just now, can you forgive me? I didn't mean you any offense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? "Ms. Paimon"... That has a nice ring to it! Alright then, the magnanimous Paimon has decided to forgive you.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Wonderful! I feel much better now. Let's meet tomorrow at <color=#00E1FFFF>Komore Teahouse</color>. I'll bring an even better script, you'll see!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's great that he's so motivated, but it's like Mr. Okazaki said... Is it really okay for him to do it all by himself?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He says he's gonna write a brand-new script in one day. That's a scary big job, isn't it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd like to help him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, maybe you should let Xavier work out the script by himself. Paimon thinks we can help him with his actor problem instead.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll go talk to the actors.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that should take a load off his back.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Well, if you're ready, we can go ahead and begin a test shot.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: You sure are straightforward.

dialogues.speaker: Sasano
dialogues.text: It's not like I want to make things difficult for Mr. Xavier... *sigh* Anyway, I hope you won't have to do it 11 times over like we had to.
